comparator.name: Criminologie
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026–2027 curriculum specifies a fixed 180-EC three-year bachelor: criminological and social-science foundations, legal study, two methods courses, three Research Lab stages, advanced criminology and criminal-law courses, a 15-EC minor, prevention and law-enforcement study, European justice, migration/diversity/crime, and a 15-EC analysis-and-reporting component. There are no formal bachelor routes requiring selection.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Legal, sociological, political and behavioural foundations precede advanced criminal-law, social-theory, psychology and research work; the sociology sequence progresses from Introduction through Modern Sociology to advanced contemporary theory, and all formal prerequisites and term offerings are satisfied.

courseTraceability.rationale: Law, Society & Justice provides foundational legal, socio-legal and normative perspectives on law, including criminal law and justice. It implements the explicit academic basis “Law, criminal justice and punishment”.

Introduction to Sociology introduces sociological concepts and theories for analysing the social causes and consequences of crime. It implements the explicit academic basis “Society, exclusion and victimisation”.

basisLabels: Crime prevention, public safety and policy evaluation

basisLabels: Psychology, social behaviour and life-course development

courseTraceability.rationale: Social Psychology examines social influence, attitudes, groups and interpersonal behaviour relevant to offending, victimisation and social reactions. It implements the explicit academic basis “Psychology, social behaviour and life-course development”.

notes.text: The Erasmus bachelor provides a dedicated criminology sequence with specialised criminological theory, crime measurement, criminal careers, formal and material criminal law, law-enforcement study and a three-stage criminology research-lab sequence. UCR can build strong crime-and-justice programmes, but it does not reproduce that full disciplinary and professional sequence.
